core.title: Default to reference execution: follow declared routes and continuations
core.given: A journey declares interlocking routes and train continuations.
core.when: You plan or document how the journey executes.
core.then: Follow the declared routes and train continuations without additional scheduling or speculative transformations.
prefer: Choose reference execution when ordering matters, the workload is small, behavior must be reproduced, or performance evidence does not justify an alternative.
Treat reference execution as the default, not a mandated slow path.
avoid: Planning reference execution as a new dispatch option in the engine that executes journeys.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration behavior from this pattern.
core.why: Reference execution is the default strategy, and it is what the current single-route continuation model supports.
evidence: The plan artifact's execution steps follow the declared routes and train continuations, with no added scheduling or speculative transformation.
Existing plan and source validators pass.
verification: Severity 3, disposition advisory: guidance only — not independent enforcement, and not a new execution-dispatch option.
The realization's existing plan and source validators apply; this convention adds no independent check of its own.
Boundary: reference execution is what the current single-route continuation model supports; unimplemented orchestration behavior cannot be inferred from this pattern.

fires: A plan artifact describes how a journey executes its declared routes and train continuations.
A planner considers adding scheduling, reordering or speculative transformations to a journey.
A journey is order-sensitive, has a small workload, or must reproduce behavior.
doesNotFire: The task does not involve journey execution, routes or continuations.
Parallelism, batching or performance is mentioned with no journey, route or continuation context.
Pure wording fix that does not describe or change how a journey executes.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds whose files the activation recognizes as describing how a journey executes; instantiating the core's file_kind fact with these kinds recovers the Bun activation.

bunOnly.reason: A shared-context id of the ATDD-Bun realization; the core states the shared content (advisory boundary, existing validators apply, no inferred orchestration behavior) generically in verification.

classification.note: Journey, interlocking route and train continuation are the shared ATDD domain model, not stack mechanics; statement kept as-is.
Planning/documenting scope is role-level; no change needed.
Single obligation kept verbatim; it names no stack, runtime or path.
The single-route continuation model is the shared execution model, not a stack fact; also carries the runtime-boundary statement of verifier_detail[0].
Applicability conditions (ordering, workload, reproduction, performance evidence) are stack-neutral.
'Runtime dispatch option' generalized to 'a new dispatch option in the engine that executes journeys'; the core may not speak of a runtime, the meaning is unchanged.
Observable restatement of the THEN; 'plan' read as the plan-artifact role.
Validators referred to generically; the core names no validator or tool ids.
Capability boundary of the shared execution model; restated neutrally as verification entry 3.
Neutral content (guidance not enforcement, existing validators apply, no inferred orchestration behavior) maps to verification entries 1-3; only the shared-context id is realization-specific.
Per-rule severity and disposition are rule data in core verification, not profile keys.
Journey-domain task terms are stack-neutral. The note's scoping (generic terms count only with journey context) is carried by core doesNotFire[1].

Neutral value is the plan-artifact role; the concrete kinds (plan, wagon, wmbt, acceptance, journey) come from the profile. The note ('planner artifacts that describe how a journey executes') is carried by core fires[0].

neutralityNotes: The convention is already almost entirely stack-neutral: journey, interlocking route, train continuation and the single-route continuation model belong to the shared ATDD domain model, so they stay in the core. 'Runtime dispatch option' (avoid[0], verifier_detail[1]) was generalized to a dispatch option in the engine that executes journeys, because the core may not name a runtime. The concrete plan-artifact kind tokens (plan, wagon, wmbt, acceptance, journey) are profile data (roles.plan_artifact.kinds, rendered as a comma-separated string), not core content; bun.json's own note treats all five as planner artifacts. The fact notes of bun.json have no core field; their content is preserved by doesNotFire[1] and fires[0]. The shared-context id and the rule's own ids remain Bun realization details.
